name: The Sunken Halls
summary: The deep-folk's oldest realm under the Stone Crown: nine clan-halls carved in the Concord's high age, sunk or sealed through the Sundering and the long silence after. Hallord is the eldest and only gate most outsiders will ever see; the rest answer to their own Keepers.

geography.character: vast carved halls, stair-streets, forge-vents, and sealed doors older than any living signer

notable_sites.name: Hallord Gate
notable_sites.note: The open hold — trade-hall, embassy, and the continent's best hammer-work.

notable_sites.name: The Sealed Ninth
notable_sites.note: A hall shut from the inside during the Sundering. Knocking has been reported. The clans do not discuss it.

notable_sites.name: The Deep Forge
notable_sites.note: Where deep-forge coal still burns; its fire predates the Edict and has never been let out.

lore_notes: The Deep Forging — Orbren teaching the hammer — is said to have happened here, in fire that has not gone out since.
Deep-folk maps of the halls are sung, not drawn; a stolen copy would be worth a kingdom and cause three wars.
adventure_hooks: A sealed door opens one inch on its own and the clan asks outsiders to stand witness — someone must be blameable if it goes wrong.
Deep-forge coal surfaces in a Hollow Mile crate; finding the shaft it leaked from means finding a hall that is not on any list.
